comparison: Both evaluate C18-C26 (PV/SST firing patterns during up/down states) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and sample sizes, while peer reviewers accept these as basic characterization without concerns.

Both address C27-C35 (phase-locking analysis). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with rigorous statistics, but peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, requesting additional characterization of phase histogram variability and heterogeneity analysis.

Both evaluate phase speed analysis (C36-C40). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with significant p-values, but peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN (along with C41-C44), requesting comparable analysis for optogenetic experiments and quantification of visual differences.

OpenEval evaluates C41-C44 (correlation analyses) as SUPPORTED with appropriate caution. Peer reviewers group these with C36-C40 in R3, marking UNCERTAIN and requesting phase speed analysis for optogenetic data.

Both address C45-C46 (hypotheses about interneuron control). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as reasonable inferences validated by optogenetics, but peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, indicating current correlative evidence is insufficient without additional characterization.
Both evaluate C47-C48 (optogenetic targeting validation) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes adequate sample sizes and specificity, while peer reviewers accept without comment.

Both address C49-C56 (PV/SST activation effects). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with highly significant p-values, but peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, requesting phase speed quantification for optogenetic experiments to determine natural control mechanisms.

Both evaluate C57-C64 (inhibition effects on state transitions). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong bidirectional control evidence, but peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, noting transition slope differences need systematic quantification and comparison to baseline.

Both address C65-C72 (differential PV vs SST effects on firing rates) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical distinctions, peer reviewers acknowledge alternative mechanisms without specific concerns.

Both evaluate C73-C74 (latency and slope differences between cell types) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes functional differences in transition control, peer reviewers acknowledge cell-type specificity as important finding. Peer R8 also includes C87-C89.

Both address mesoscale effects (C75-C77). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by dual illumination methods, but peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN (R9 includes C75-C82, C95, C100), requesting quantification of temporal dynamics and time lags.

Both evaluate dual patch-clamp recordings (C78-C81). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with significant p-values, but peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, stating difficulty assessing time lags and requesting additional synchronicity analysis.

Both address mesoscale control conclusions (C82, C95, C100). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by convergent multi-method evidence, but peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, requesting quantification of temporal dynamics from Figure 6.
Both evaluate C83 (down state control mechanism) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval views as reasonable inference from optogenetic data, peer reviewers acknowledge as novel finding about down state dynamics.

Both address C84-C86 (cell number estimates and sensitivity). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate qualification, peer reviewers accept quantitative estimates without question. Peer R10 also addresses C86 regarding sensitivity.

Both evaluate C87-C89 (differential effects between interneuron types) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and physiological transitions, peer reviewers acknowledge cell-type specificity and alternative mechanisms.

Both address C90-C91 (mechanistic interpretations). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN as speculative without direct testing, peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED, accepting as reasonable speculation without challenge.

Both evaluate main conclusions (C92-C94). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by convergent evidence, peer reviewers also mark SUPPORTED (R11 includes C92-C94, C101-C102), affirming important contributions while requesting strengthening analysis.
Both address experimental approach (C96-C99) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes multi-method strength, peer reviewers praise the non-purely-optogenetic approach and characterization effort.

Both evaluate overarching conclusions (C101-C102) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive evidence integration, peer reviewers affirm overall conclusions about bidirectional control and novel findings.

Both address background claims (C1-C8). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED as established context from literature, peer reviewers also mark SUPPORTED (R15 includes C1-C17), noting appropriate discussion of recent studies.

Both evaluate prior conflicting evidence (C9-C17) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes fair characterization of field controversy, peer reviewers accept literature context and discussion of thalamus versus cortical circuits.
